title: Changelog
html:
Changelog

All notable changes to wikicc are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning. Entries describe what a user of the binary can observe, not how the change was implemented; the rules behind them live in docs/design.md.

[1.0.0] - 2026-11-03

First stable release: the features the reader offers.

Reader

  • Compile a folder of Markdown documents into a self-contained reader that needs no server, no sibling files and no network.
  • Search over titles, headings and body text, including CJK.
  • Link graph of the folder with zoom, pan and drag; a plain left click opens the document of the node.
  • Chapter outline of the current document, following the section being read.
  • Block references: pointing at a chapter of another document previews that chapter, and the preview can be pinned and dragged out of the way. A chapter that does not exist is reported as a broken reference and explained.
  • Tables with sorting and Excel-style per-column filtering.
  • Light and dark themes, and a layout that stays usable down to phone width.

Markdown support

  • GitHub-flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, strikethrough and footnotes.
  • Nested chapters with stable, Unicode-aware heading anchors, so CJK headings keep their text.
  • Chapter links that address one chapter of another document ([label](doc.md#chapter)) or the document as a whole.
  • Reference-style links ([[n]] plus a reference list) alongside ordinary Markdown links, and a reference list rendered for the styles that use it.
  • Fenced code highlighting, done at build time.
  • Mermaid diagrams from a fence tagged mermaid.
  • Raw HTML inside Markdown, passed through unchanged; the input is trusted, so untrusted documents must not be compiled.

Output

  • Two output formats: single-html (one page with everything inlined, opens by double click from any directory) and html-dir (a page plus an assets/ folder, ready to be copied, zipped or served as it is).
  • Assets addressed by content, so identical bytes are stored once no matter how many documents reference them.
  • Nothing is fetched at runtime: no CDN, no web font, no remote stylesheet.
  • Two builds of the same input produce byte-identical artifacts.

Executable

  • One binary with no runtime dependencies: on Windows it carries the project logo as an icon in the file explorer.
  • Statically linked release archives for Linux and Windows, so neither needs runtime packages on the machine that runs it.
